solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What swine exhibits, trampling on one in model of adoration? Nothing

definitions.text: What swine exhibits, trampling on one in model of adoration? Nothing

indicators.note: to trample on something is to stamp it out and stand in its place, so one letter is pushed out and another takes its spot

blocks.note: Cupid, the god of love, is the figure that stands for adoration
a boar is a male pig
I is the Roman numeral for one; it is the letter pushed out of CUPID
love means nil, a score of nothing in tennis

explanation.surface: A greedy pig blunders into a statue of Cupid, and the question is what affection it really has to offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trampling on' means the pig stands where the one used to be. The whole clue is also the definition: a pig fond only of whoever feeds it shows exactly this.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names affection that is shown only in hope of food or reward, which is all a hungry farm animal offers its keeper.

clue.text: In the lab they detect my e-reference?

blocks.note: first meaning: sealed vessels of supersaturated vapour in which charged particles leave visible trails
second meaning: the setter's favourite dictionary, consulted online rather than on paper

explanation.walkthrough: Chambers is the dictionary most British setters use, and the cloud is where online services live, so the setter's online Chambers is a cloud Chambers. The question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists used these vapour-filled devices to see the tracks of subatomic particles; the positron was discovered with one in 1932.

clue.text: In sequence, 16 7 perhaps for El Greco sculpture?

blocks.note: pi is the sixteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Two numbers look like cross-references to other answers, offered as a description of some Greek painter's statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 and 7 look like references to 16-across and 7-down, but 'for El Greco' (a Greek, for whom letters run in Greek order) says to count through the Greek alphabet instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pietà is a sculpture or painting of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ, most famously Michelangelo's in St Peter's, Rome.

clue.text: Bananas out of this world

blocks.note: first meaning: crazy, out of touch with reality
second meaning: literally located somewhere other than Earth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' as slang for mad is the trick; read with the rest it looks like fruit that is wonderful, but the two parts are separate senses of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone said to live elsewhere in the solar system is figuratively detached from reality, and literally would be beyond Earth.

clue.text: Find new job for retired English police chief, nursing Beecham’s baby

indicators.note: to retire is to draw back, so the letters go backwards
to nurse is to hold close in the arms, so one piece cradles another

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
short for superintendent, a senior police officer
the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, founded by the conductor Sir Thomas Beecham in 1946

explanation.surface: Someone needs a fresh job for a pensioned-off senior English police officer who is now looking after a famous man's infant.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPER is British shorthand for a police superintendent. Beecham's 'baby' is the orchestra he created, the Royal Philharmonic, abbreviated RPO.
explanation.definitionFit: To repurpose something is to adapt it for a different use, giving it another role to perform.

clue.text: Before school, lecturer split

blocks.note: L is a standard abbreviation for lecturer
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A university teacher breaks away or quits just before the school term starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before school' places the lecturer's letter ahead of the school. 'Split' is not about breaking up but British slang for informing or telling tales.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to split on someone is to inform or reveal a secret, and the phrasal verb means disclosing what should stay hidden.

clue.text: Fat bottom within reach in swing

indicators.note: something placed in a thing sits inside its outer letters

blocks.note: something within reach can be got, so it is getable
butt is slang for the buttocks
to veer is to swing suddenly in direction

explanation.surface: A large backside is easy to reach while someone sits on a playground swing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, the bottom piece sits at the bottom, below the 'within reach' piece; both then go inside the word for swing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shea and cocoa butter are solid fats pressed from plants, so the phrase is a name for a kind of fat.

clue.text: Displaying a boxing poster that appears to be substandard

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, as goods are packed in a carton

blocks.note: 'a' means one, as in a single item
par is the standard score in golf; 'sub' says it sits above whatever goes under it
a poster is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: A boxing poster looks shoddy, like something printed on the cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sub' means under: in a down entry the poster appears under the standard, so it is sub-standard. 'Boxing poster' looks like a fight bill, but boxing is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops on parade are lined up in public view, and figuratively anything showing itself off is being put on display.

clue.text: In bits 7, and missing performance

indicators.note: something in bits has been broken up, so the letters are scattered into a new order
what is missing is absent, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: the answer to 7-down
taken as written, and removed

explanation.surface: A show is described as fragmentary and lacking something.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference supplies the letters of 7-down; take out A, N and D and rearrange the five that remain.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged musical drama, and a staging of one is a performance; the word can also mean a production of that kind.

clue.text: Panama adopts a label attached to independent S American region

indicators.note: to adopt is to take into one's family, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: PA is the international code for Panama
taken as written
a tag is a label
attached to means on, as a label is on a parcel
I is the standard abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: A Central American country takes in a branded region of South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama' tempts one to think of hats or the canal, but it supplies its two-letter code, which then wraps round everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Patagonia is the vast southern tip of the continent, shared between Argentina and Chile.

clue.text: Tape underwear to bustle? It’s not been done before

indicators.note: to bustle is to move about busily, so the letters are rushed into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tapes their underwear onto a Victorian bustle, an innovation no one has tried before.
explanation.walkthrough: A bustle was a padded frame worn under a skirt at the back, which helps the picture; here it is the verb that stirs up the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unprecedented is a change of direction from established practice, a novel course never previously taken.

clue.text: Make it big in the lion-exporting business?

definitions.text: Make it big in the lion-exporting business?

blocks.note: surface reading: become very successful commercially
setter's reading: a firm dealing in big cats, whose stock makes a lot of noise

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for brisk, profitable business is taken literally: a trade in lions would be full of roaring.
explanation.definitionFit: To make it big in commerce is to sell a lot very quickly, which the idiom describes as a business going loudly well.

clue.text: PM hours during which I have to dine

indicators.note: what happens during a period falls within it, so the span surrounds the action

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hour, doubled for the plural
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the evening hours when they are obliged to sit down to dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like afternoon, matching 'hours', but it stands for Prime Minister. The two hours bracket the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Heath was the British Conservative Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974.

clue.text: Employed in restaurant, ever taking tip?

indicators.note: something employed in a place works inside it, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the run of letters across the end of the first word and the whole second
its first letter completes the run

explanation.surface: A waiter working in a restaurant always accepts a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like the gratuity a waiter gets, but it is the verb meaning tilt. The answer runs across three words, ending on the first letter of the third.
explanation.definitionFit: Antevert is a medical and technical word for tilting an organ or object forward, so it means to tip it.

clue.text: MD’s position, in the main?

blocks.note: first meaning, split in two: a managing director sits above the board of directors
second meaning: fallen from a ship into the sea, the main being an old word for the ocean

explanation.walkthrough: MD looks medical but is managing director. 'In the main' reads as 'mostly', yet the main is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has gone off the side of a vessel is in the open ocean, and a chief executive ranks above company directors.

clue.text: Club employee starts to sense trouble after rolling dice, say?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first of each is kept
rolled things tumble over, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: the opening letters of these two words
taken as written

explanation.surface: A casino worker gets a bad feeling just after the dice have been thrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a gaming club with dice, but it is a strip club. 'Say' is not an example marker here; its letters are part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecdysiast is H. L. Mencken's jokey learned word for a striptease artist, someone working at a strip club.

clue.text: Rockers heading for bird under protection of rival?

indicators.note: what is under someone's protection is sheltered inside their care

blocks.note: Mods were the 1960s British youth tribe who fought the Rockers
heading for a place means going to it
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: A bird is being steered under a rival's wing for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1960s Britain the Mods (scooters, suits) and the Rockers (motorbikes, leather) were rival youth gangs, so the Rockers' rival is a mod.
explanation.definitionFit: Motörhead were Lemmy's heavy rock band, so as a plural group of musicians they are rockers.

clue.text: ’Ow’re thee stalling Wensleydale’s most common lech?

indicators.note: to stall something is to keep it in a stall or pen, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: Ey up is a Yorkshire greeting meaning roughly how are you
E occurs three times in Wensleydale, more than any other letter

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire voice asks how a lecherous man is getting on, perhaps over a lump of the local cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Wensleydale is a Yorkshire dale famous for its crumbly cheese, which sets the dialect scene; here it is just a word whose commonest letter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To lech after someone is to look at them with obvious desire, which is what ogling a person in this way means.

clue.text: Volunteer packing for RSPB? He’s left — off for some excitement?

definitions.text: Volunteer packing for RSPB? He’s left — off for some excitement?

indicators.note: packing is the stuffing inside, so only the inner letters are kept
excited things are stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the inner letters of the bird charity's initials
the inner letter
the inner letters
the inner letter

explanation.surface: A charity volunteer filling envelopes for a bird society quits, wanting a more thrilling way to spend time.
explanation.walkthrough: The RSPB is the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds, a big British charity that relies on volunteers. The whole clue also defines: a mailing-room helper who might well leave for livelier work.
explanation.definitionFit: Charities send out appeals by post, and the unpaid helper who fills and seals that mail is doing famously dull work.

clue.text: Uncle Sam’s father appropriately kicked about literary leaves

indicators.note: whatever leaves goes away, so those letters are removed
a thing kicked about is knocked around, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, every one of its letters taken out

explanation.surface: An American's dad is suitably booted around over some pages of a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literary leaves' looks like book pages, but the word literary departs, letter by letter, from the long word, and the five left are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam personifies the USA, so his father is an American father, and this is a US informal word for dad.

clue.text: You need this mufti’s judgement to get off at Waterloo

indicators.note: the letters needed form part of a longer run, and must be picked out from inside it

blocks.note: the run across the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A Muslim scholar's ruling is needed before a train passenger can alight at London's Waterloo station.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo is a major London railway station, so the surface is about a commuter. The answer spans three words, from the last letter of the first to the first two of the last.
explanation.definitionFit: A mufti is a Muslim legal scholar, and his formal ruling on a point of Islamic law is called by this name.

clue.text: Legume gratins supply crusts exercise

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, it means bending freely, so the letters flex into a new order
a crust is an outer covering, so one piece forms the shell round another

blocks.note: taken as written
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Baked dishes with crunchy tops provide some exercise, said of a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like the verb provide, but it is the adverb from supple, so it signals a rearrangement; 'crusts' is a verb meaning forms a crust round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea whose pods have tough strings along their seams is a kind of leguminous vegetable.

clue.text: Individual plated meat at our homes

indicators.note: something that homes in a place lives inside it, so the letters dwell within the words

blocks.note: the run from the end of the first word through the second into the third

explanation.surface: A single serving of meat is put on a plate in our houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plated' looks like food served on a plate, but it means armour-plated, and the individual is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The tatou is an armadillo, an animal covered in bony armour plates, so it is a plated creature.

clue.text: Cooking task: rare, recipe-light, treat?

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement
light means lacking, as in a pound light, so a letter is short

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for recipe on prescriptions, the one letter taken out

explanation.surface: A kitchen job with an underdone, low-calorie dish as the reward.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one R from the thirteen letters before rearranging. The joke is that this dish needs no cooking at all and is served raw, rarer than rare.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw minced beef with egg yolk and capers is a delicacy, a dish served as a special indulgence.
